tasks.prof.text.fast_scan: Scans the 100 most popular ports and detects service versions and the operating system (OS). Suited to a quick look at which ports are open.
tasks.prof.text.intense: A full scan that detects the operating system (OS) and service versions, runs the default scripts and runs a traceroute.
tasks.prof.text.discovery: Finds the devices that are online in the network without scanning ports. Suited to mapping a network.
tasks.prof.text.custom: Add nmap options of your own to suit the target.
tasks.prof.text.vuln_scan: A full scan (OS and service versions), then looks up vulnerabilities (CVE) for the versions found in the NVD database. Needs an internet connection.
tasks.adv.title: Advanced Options
tasks.adv.summary: Timing, ping, ports, DNS, gentle, UDP
tasks.adv.timing_card_text: Faster levels wait less for replies and retry less often, so on a slow network or one that loses packets they may miss some ports or devices.
tasks.adv.timing_t2: Highly accurate, and gentle on devices that handle little load
tasks.adv.timing_t3: A balance of speed and accuracy
tasks.adv.timing_t4: Fast; results are usually close to T3 on a stable internal network
tasks.adv.timing_card_foot: If the results look incomplete, scan again at a slower level.
tasks.adv.pn_help: Treat every IP as online. Use when devices block ping.
tasks.adv.pn_card: nmap scans the ports of every address without first checking whether it answers ping. Use it when devices block ping and a normal scan finds nothing. It takes much longer on a wide target and accepts at most 1,024 addresses. Only devices with evidence of a reply are shown, such as an open port, a closed port or a MAC address.
tasks.adv.mc_aria: About device names from mDNS / SSDP
tasks.adv.mc_help: Ask devices on the same network as the computer running the system for their name and model
tasks.adv.mc_card: During the scan the system sends mDNS (Bonjour) and SSDP (UPnP) queries and listens for replies. Devices that support them report their own name and model. It works only on the network the computer running the system is connected to.
tasks.adv.ap_help: Checks 65,535 ports instead of the usual list; takes much longer
tasks.adv.ap_card: Checks all 65,535 TCP ports instead of the usual list (Fast Scan 100 ports, Intense Scan and Vulnerability Scan 1,000 ports), so it may find services on ports outside that list. It takes much longer and sends many packets, so an intrusion detection system (IDS) may raise an alert. At most 64 addresses are accepted. A device that takes more than 45 minutes is skipped and its ports are shown as unknown. The system stops a job that runs longer than 6 hours, and that job has no scan result.
tasks.adv.dns_help: Faster; internal IPs are not sent to DNS, but DNS names will be missing
tasks.adv.dns_card: Neither nmap nor the system asks a DNS server what name each IP address has, so the scan is faster and internal IP addresses are not sent to a DNS server. The scan result will have no DNS names. NetBIOS names, which are asked from the device itself, can still be read. The devices and ports found do not change.
tasks.adv.pr: Find devices that do not answer ping
tasks.adv.pr_aria: About finding devices that do not answer ping
tasks.adv.pr_help: Sends packets to common ports to find devices that block ping
tasks.adv.pr_card: Before scanning, nmap sends TCP packets to common ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 445, 3389, 8080) in addition to the normal ping, to find devices that block ping. Unlike -Pn, it does not treat every address as online. It helps when the target is on another subnet (through a router); on the same subnet nmap already uses ARP, so nothing changes. It takes a little longer. An intrusion detection system (IDS) may treat it as a scan, so please tell the security team before using it on a wide range. It cannot be combined with -Pn.
tasks.adv.gt_help: Sends packets much more slowly to reduce the load on devices and the network
tasks.adv.gt_card: For devices that handle little load or links with low bandwidth. Sends packets much more slowly: speed T2, at most 50 packets per second in total, at most 2 retries, and devices that take more than 45 minutes are skipped. Roughly 10 to 40 times slower than normal. At most 1,024 addresses are accepted. The system stops a job that runs longer than 8 hours, and that job has no scan result. Intense Scan and Vulnerability Scan do not run the default NSE scripts of -A (the system does not keep script results anyway) but still detect versions, the operating system and traceroute. It cannot be combined with scanning all ports, and it uses T2 instead of the Timing option.
tasks.adv.udp_help: Scans the UDP ports of the devices found in a second round; takes longer
tasks.adv.udp_scope_help_common: 12 ports chosen for network equipment, such as SNMP, SIP, NTP and IPMI. The fastest choice, and it also reads the service name and version.
tasks.adv.udp_scope_help_top100: nmap's top 100 UDP ports. Usually a few minutes per device, at most 15. Service versions are not detected.
tasks.adv.udp_scope_help_top1000: nmap's top 1,000 UDP ports. Can take tens of minutes per device, at most 45, and at most 32 addresses are accepted. Service versions are not detected. Not available with the Gentle scan or timing T1.
tasks.adv.udp_card: After the first scan finishes, the system runs a second scan of UDP on the IPv4 devices that the first scan found online, on 12 common ports: 53, 67, 69, 123, 137, 161, 500, 520, 623, 1434, 1900, 5060 (for example DNS, SNMP, NTP, SIP). The TCP results do not change. A UDP port that does not reply is shown as open|filtered, which means it is not known whether it is open or filtered; it is not an open port, and most ports are shown this way. Vulnerability Scan looks up CVEs only for UDP ports that are open. The system must run with Administrator or root rights and have Npcap. At most 64 addresses are accepted (the whole range entered is counted, not only the devices that are online). It takes much longer. The system stops a job that runs longer than 6 hours for both rounds together (8 hours when the gentle scan is on).
tasks.adv.udp_card_top: Choose Top 100 or Top 1,000 to scan more UDP ports instead of the 12. The ranking is nmap's own, from how often a UDP port is found open on the internet. It is not chosen for telecom equipment, so ports that such equipment uses may not be included (for example GTP). Neither choice detects service versions. A Top 1,000 job is stopped after 8 hours. A device that runs over its time limit gets no UDP result and is shown as unknown. When more than 25 ports share one state, nmap does not list them one by one, so a device can show no UDP ports although many gave no answer.
tasks.adv.vi_card: The higher the value, the more probe methods nmap uses to identify the version of a service, so more is identified but it takes longer. If a service does not reveal its version, raising this does not help. The default is 7.
tasks.js.note.discovery: Checks which devices are online (ping sweep); does not scan ports
tasks.js.note.fast_scan: Scans the popular ports (100) and detects service versions and the operating system
tasks.js.note.intense: Detailed scan: operating system, versions, default scripts and traceroute (-A)
tasks.js.note.vuln_scan: Scans in detail like an Intense Scan, then looks up CVEs in NVD for the versions of the open services
tasks.js.note.custom: Scans with arguments set by the user (checked against the allowed list)
tasks.js.note.xml_upload: Imported from an nmap XML file; nothing was scanned
tasks.js.step.gateway_probe: If the default gateway of the computer running the system is inside the scanned range but does not answer ping, the system checks its ports 53, 80, 443 and 8080 again
tasks.js.step.mdns_ssdp: Listens for mDNS (Bonjour) and SSDP (UPnP) replies during the scan
tasks.js.step.nvd_lookup: Looks up CVEs for the open ports through the NVD API (only for services whose product and version nmap could identify)
tasks.js.step.udp_pass: Second round: scans 12 common UDP ports on the devices the first round found online
tasks.js.step.udp_pass_top100: Second round: scans nmap's top 100 UDP ports on the devices the first round found online
tasks.js.step.udp_pass_top1000: Second round: scans nmap's top 1,000 UDP ports on the devices the first round found online
tasks.js.step.xml_import: The data comes from the imported file; no scan packets were sent to the network
